title: Low Step-In Dog Beds
seo_title: Low Step-In Dog Beds for Stiff & Older Dogs | PawLunova
seo_description: Dog beds with a low way in: a low oval profile, a dropped front or an open corner, on memory foam or egg-crate foam. 100 nights at home to decide.

image.alt: Low step-in dog beds: the black and cream Coniston dog bed on a living-room rug

intro_html: Easy in, easy out for stiff morning legs. Each bed here has a low way in, from a low oval profile to a dropped front or an open corner, so there's no high wall to climb.
description_html:
There comes a point where a deep-walled bed stops being cosy and starts being an obstacle. You see it in the pause at the edge before they get in, and the effort of getting out on a cold morning. Every bed in this collection keeps the way in low, so stepping in takes less out of them.

How the way in differs from bed to bed

Coniston is an oval memory foam bed that sits close to the floor, with a rim for a chin. Newlands, Easedale and Burnmoor keep a bolster on all four sides but drop the front section, with profiled egg-crate foam underneath. Braithwaite has a bolstered edge with one corner cut open, so they can walk straight in.

All five have a waterproof liner or lining around the foam, and each product page sets out its sizing and exactly what is inside.

Can a bed fix stiff joints?

No, and we won't pretend otherwise. A bed is for comfort, not a treatment, and if your dog is in pain or finding it hard to move, your vet is the right person to ask. What a low way in changes is the effort of getting on and off the bed, several times a day.

What if it isn't right for them?

You have 100 nights at home to decide. If they don't settle on it, we collect it free from the UK mainland and refund you in full. One trial per household; damage and other exclusions apply. See how the trial works.

For more beds with foam underneath, see orthopaedic dog beds or dog beds for older dogs.
